_what_this_is: What the Zenodo record at `published_doi` ACTUALLY CONTAINS, as published, plus any version that has been DRAFTED but not yet published. Not what the repository contains now — that is fusion-junction-aso-archive-manifest.json, which moves with every commit. This file moves only when a version is drafted or published on Zenodo, and publishing is an irreversible act. ⚠ IT IS NO LONGER 'THE AUTHOR PERFORMS IT BY HAND': as of 2026-08-30 the loop may publish a Zenodo deposition under a standing grant plus a per-publication approval, enforced by `zenodo_deposit.refuse_unless_publishable`. What did NOT change is the irreversibility, or that the approval is per deposition — an approval for one publication is never an approval for the next.
_what_the_superseded_list_is: Every version this record has published, newest FIRST in `published` and older ones here, each with the provenance it carried while it was current. ⛔ THEY ARE KEPT BECAUSE A ZENODO VERSION IS IMMUTABLE AND STILL RESOLVES: a reader holding an old DOI out of an old copy of the paper gets those files forever, so 'what did 22061075 actually contain' stays an answerable question rather than becoming one only git archaeology can settle. Nothing here is a live state — `published` is the only block any gate reads.
_why_this_exists: Round 15, 2026-08-22. Three independent reviewers found the same defect from three directions: the submitted manuscript's Data and code availability says 'the archived copy is the citable one', and the archived copy was 16 files behind the repository — including the extended report itself, whose deposited text still carried two statements this repository had since corrected (the void-test definition, and a claim that the dinucleotide-preserving scramble holds the 5' guanine run). It shipped unnoticed because NOTHING RECORDED WHAT WAS DEPOSITED. `--check-archive` compares the manifest to the working tree, so it turns green exactly as the tree walks away from the deposit, and `archive_content_digest` is stored only inside the manifest that computes it, so it can never disagree with itself.
_the_window_this_file_exists_to_make_leg: Between drafting a corrected version and publishing it, the papers cite a DOI that is not yet live and the published record is still the old one. That gap is deliberate and is the whole point of the reserve-then-rebuild ordering: the manuscript must print the identifier the archive will carry BEFORE the files are frozen, because a published version cannot be edited. `pending` records the drafted version so the gap is a stated state rather than a disagreement nobody can see.
_how_to_update: When the pending version is PUBLISHED: move its doi/digest/n_files/git_revision up into `published`, set `published.published` to the date, and delete `pending`. When a new version is DRAFTED: set `pending`. AND READ THE RECORD BACK BEFORE WRITING `published` — `record=verify` on deposit-zenodo.yml does it with no token. 'The publish step reported success' is a report about an outside system; 'the DOI printed in the papers resolves to a published record' is a reading, and this repository has already paid three days for the difference (the bioRxiv status that stayed ⏳ after the rejection). NEVER edit either block to silence a gate — the gate is the whole point, and a green gate on a stale deposit is what this file was created to end.
